title: Add multi-armed-bandit-based canary evaluator for churn-resilient regression detection
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds a Bayesian multi-armed-bandit evaluator that dynamically weights multiple canary detectors to reduce false positives during traffic churn; includes metrics, dashboards, tests, and a safe rollout path.
description: Problem: periodic traffic churn (traffic spikes, A/B experiments, client-side batching changes) has caused an elevated rate of false-positive canary detections during large rollouts, triggering unnecessary rollbacks. Motivation: decrease noisy rollbacks while preserving sensitivity to true regressions. Approach: implement a lightweight multi-armed-bandit (MAB) evaluator that treats independent detection heuristics as arms (latency-percentile fingerprint, throughput-drop detector, error-spike detector, and context-aware drift signal). The evaluator uses Thompson sampling to adaptively weight detectors per-customer and per-traffic-shape, and exposes a confidence score to the existing rollout guard. When confidence is low (high disagreement across arms or low sample counts), the guard will delay automatic rollback and instead create a high-fidelity probe (increased sampling + targeted synthetic traffic). This PR adds: 1) core MAB evaluation service (stateless per-window evaluator with periodic posterior updates), 2) adapter layer to surface MAB confidence to existing canary pipeline, 3) telemetry (per-arm posterior traces, decision reasons), 4) dashboards and alert rules that surface low-confidence decisions, 5) unit/integration tests and an e2e synthetic traffic harness, 6) a migration script to backfill historical detector outputs for model calibration. Backwards compatibility: existing rollout guards keep current behavior but will read the new confidence field; default rollout policy unchanged until rollout flag is enabled. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on canary teams; start with 5% of rollouts for 48 hours, expand to 25% after no regression in 24h, then global. Safety: when the MAB reports high-confidence regression, we keep the same automatic rollback behavior. Related work: builds on ENG-2748 (detector fusion framework) and PM-78 (reduce noisy rollbacks initiative). Tests: added deterministic unit tests for Thompson sampler, property tests for posterior updates, integration tests that run detectors in parallel with synthetic churn traces, and an e2e canary run against a staging fleet. Observability: Grafana dashboard panels for per-arm regret, confidence histogram, and decision trace; prometheus metrics prefixed perf_canary_mab_. CI: initial run showed flakey perf-canary-e2e due to timing in synthetic harness; fixed by making probe timeouts relative to observed baseline and re-ran. Performance: evaluator adds negligible CPU (microservice using async worker); memory bounded by a configurable window (default 10 minutes). Implementation notes: prefer 64-bit floats for posteriors to avoid numerical drift; store minimal state in Redis with TTL to support failover. Migration: backfill script runs weekly for two runs to seed priors; can be skipped for small tenants. Security/permissions: read-only to canary outputs, no change to customer data paths. Link to test harness: internal:perf-canary/mab-e2e. Potential follow-ups: add per-tenant priors, ML-trained arm weighting, and automated canary-to-A/B promotion for low-confidence cases.
